# Audio buses and effects

Status: design, open for review, planned for BlitzLLVM 2.0 (Xaymar, 25 Nov 2026). Nothing here is implemented yet; the
implementation follows in separate PRs, one per phase below.

## Why

A user asked for a "per-scene" effect mix: one place to say "everything in this cave echoes", "the world is muffled
while the pause menu is open" or "this level has stronger doppler", instead of changing every sound by hand. Today a
program can only set the volume, pan and pitch of single channels, plus the three numbers of `CreateListener`.

The case that started it: a game with planet-side and space segments. On the planet the user wants real doppler, a
rolloff that fits walking distances and a world scale in meters; in space the same settings sound wrong (a passing ship
should barely shift, distances are much larger, and there is no air to muffle or carry anything). There is no
`FreeListener` and no command that changes the listener's numbers, so the planet setup stays for the whole program.
Switching the whole listener setup when the scene changes is the first thing this design has to make easy.

The goal: a small set of Blitz-style commands for buses (groups of channels with one volume), effects on those buses
(reverb, echo, filters and a few others) and listener-wide 3D settings that can be changed at any time. Programs that
don't use the new commands must sound exactly as they do now.

## What exists today

### The original Blitz3D 1.118 and BlitzPlus

The audio commands are `LoadSound`, `Load3DSound`, `SoundVolume/Pan/Pitch`, `LoopSound`, `PlaySound`, `PlayMusic`,
`PlayCDTrack`, the `Channel*` commands, and in Blitz3D `CreateListener` and `EmitSound`. `CreateListener` passes its
rolloff, doppler and distance factors to FMOD 3.75 once (`gxAudio::set3dOptions` in `gxruntime/gxaudio.cpp`), and with
the debugger on a second `CreateListener` stops with *Listener already created*.

There is a way out that nobody documents: the listener is an entity, and `FreeEntity` on it (or on its parent) clears
the runtime's `listener` pointer (`erase` in `bbruntime/bbblitz3d.cpp`). After that, `CreateListener` works again and
passes its new numbers to FMOD. `~Listener` only moves FMOD's listener back to the origin; the rolloff, doppler and
distance factors stay at their last values until the next `CreateListener`. So switching setups works in the original as
`FreeEntity listener : listener = CreateListener(camera, r, d, s)`, but only as a full rebuild, and `EmitSound` with no
listener stops with *No Listener created* in debug builds in between.

FMOD 3 had reverb and DirectX 8
effects, but Blitz never exposed them: there is no way to add an effect or to group channels.

### blitz3d_soloud

The SoLoud port of Blitz3D (`third_party/blitz3d_soloud/bbruntime/bbaudio_soloud.cpp`) exposes the same command list as
the original and nothing more. SoLoud itself has buses and filters (biquad resonant, echo, Freeverb, lofi, flanger,
wave shaper, EQ, bass boost, DC removal, robotize, FFT), but that port never made them reachable from Blitz code.

### BlitzLLVM

The runtime (`code_runtime/source/sound.c`) does **not** use SoLoud. It plays through SDL3_mixer
(`third_party/SDL_mixer`): one `MIX_Mixer` on the default device, one `MIX_Track` per channel, panning through
`MIX_SetTrackStereo`, 3D volume, panning and doppler worked out by the runtime itself (`bb_channel_follow`, with the
10 ms doppler smoothing of #558), and the falloff curves of `SetFalloff`/`SetChannelFalloff`. `bb_create_listener`
replaces the listener and its three numbers on every call, without the debugger's error, and the numbers outlive a
`FreeEntity` of the listener, as in the original. The free-and-recreate route therefore works here too, but it also
resets the listener's measured speed, so moving sounds lose their doppler shift for a frame.

SDL3_mixer has no effects of its own. What it does have, and what this design builds on:

| SDL3_mixer feature | What it gives us |
| --- | --- |
| `MIX_Group`, `MIX_SetTrackGroup` | Tracks mixed together into one buffer per group. A track is in one group at a time. |
| `MIX_SetGroupPostMixCallback` | Read and change a group's mixed audio before it goes into the final mix. |
| `MIX_SetPostMixCallback` | Read and change the final mix before it goes to the device. |
| `MIX_SetTrackCookedCallback` | Read a track's audio after gain and pitch, before panning. Used for sends. |
| `MIX_PauseTag`/`MIX_SetTagGain` | Pause or change the gain of tagged tracks. Not needed: we track bus membership ourselves. |
| `MIX_LockMixer` | Stops the audio thread while the bus graph is changed. |

All mixing is in 32-bit float. The device may have more than two channels (`MIX_CreateMixerDevice` with a `NULL`
spec takes the device's own format), so every effect has to handle any channel count.

One detail of `MixerCallback` (`src/SDL_mixer.c`) shapes the design: a group's buffer is added to the final mix only up
to the length its tracks produced (`group_bytes`). Once the last sound of a group stops, `group_bytes` is 0 and anything
an effect wrote into that group's buffer is dropped. A reverb or echo on a group would be cut off the moment its last
sound ends. So effects can't simply run inside the group callback; see *How it is mixed* below.

## Commands

Handles follow the usual rules: 0 is "none" or "the master bus" as stated, an invalid handle is a runtime error, and
`Free*` on 0 does nothing. Numbers are floats unless noted. Constants for effect types go into a shipped include,
`Include "<audio.bb>"`, with the `BB_` prefix (#622, #639); the plain numbers work without it.

### Buses

A bus is a group of channels with its own volume, pause state and effect chain. Bus 0 is the master bus: every channel
is on it unless moved, and its effects apply to everything that plays. Buses can feed other buses, so a program can
build "world → master" and "music → master", or "cave → world → master".

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bus = CreateAudioBus([parent=0])` | New bus that feeds `parent`. |
| `FreeAudioBus bus` | Its channels and child buses move to its parent; its effects are freed. |
| `AudioBusParent bus, parent` | Feeds the bus into another one. A loop is a runtime error. |
| `AudioBusVolume bus, volume#[, fade_ms%=0]` | 0 to 1 (higher allowed, then clipped by the limiter if one is on the master). Fades linearly. |
| `PauseAudioBus bus` / `ResumeAudioBus bus` | Pauses or resumes every channel on the bus and its children. |
| `StopAudioBus bus` | Stops every channel on the bus and its children. |
| `ChannelBus channel, bus` | Moves a playing channel to a bus. |
| `SoundBus sound, bus` | The bus that channels played from this sound start on (like `SoundVolume` sets their volume). |
| `ChannelSend channel, bus, level#` | Also sends the channel to another bus at `level` (0 removes it), for shared reverbs. Up to 4 sends per channel. |

`PauseAudioBus` and `PauseChannel` stack: a channel paused on its own stays paused when its bus resumes.

### Effects

Effects sit in a chain on a bus or a channel and run in the order they were added. Parameters are numbered constants (decided, see
*Decisions*): a number is faster to look up than a name, and `Include "<audio.bb>"` gives every number a name, so code
reads like `AudioEffectParam echo, BB_EFFECTPARAM_DELAY, 0.3`.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `effect = AddAudioEffect(bus, type[, position=-1])` | Adds an effect to the bus' chain, at the end or before `position`. |
| `effect = AddChannelEffect(channel, type[, position=-1])` | The same for one channel, e.g. a low-pass for a sound behind a wall. |
| `FreeAudioEffect effect` | Removes it. A reverb's tail is cut. |
| `AudioEffectParam effect, param%, value#[, fade_ms%=0]` | Sets a parameter, fading linearly over `fade_ms`. A parameter the effect doesn't have is a runtime error. |
| `value# = GetAudioEffectParam(effect, param%)` | The value it is at (or fading to). |
| `AudioEffectBypass effect, bypass%` | Turns it off and on without losing its settings. Tails ring out. |

The parameter numbers are shared by all effects: `BB_EFFECTPARAM_FREQUENCY` is 2 for the low-pass and the shelves
alike, so there are 18 parameter constants instead of one set per effect. Each effect accepts only its own. Neither
parameter numbers nor effect types use 0, and 0 is a runtime error that suggests the include: Blitz turns a misspelt or
not-included `BB_` name into a new variable that is 0, which would otherwise quietly set the wrong parameter.

| Parameter | Constant | Parameter | Constant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 mix | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_MIX` | 10 predelay | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_PREDELAY` |
| 2 frequency | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_FREQUENCY` | 11 threshold | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_THRESHOLD` |
| 3 resonance | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_RESONANCE` | 12 ratio | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_RATIO` |
| 4 gain | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_GAIN` | 13 attack | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_ATTACK` |
| 5 delay | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_DELAY` | 14 release | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_RELEASE` |
| 6 feedback | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_FEEDBACK` | 15 ceiling | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_CEILING` |
| 7 damping | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_DAMPING` | 16 drive | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_DRIVE` |
| 8 size | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_SIZE` | 17 rate | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_RATE` |
| 9 width | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_WIDTH` | 18 bits | `BB_EFFECTPARAM_BITS` |

Every effect has `BB_EFFECTPARAM_MIX` (0 dry to 1 fully processed, default 1). Effect types for the first version, with
SoLoud's set as a guide for what Blitz programs are likely to want (parameters by their constant without the
`BB_EFFECTPARAM_` prefix):

| Type | Constant | Parameters (default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Low-pass | `BB_EFFECT_LOWPASS` | `FREQUENCY` Hz (20000), `RESONANCE` Q (0.707) |
| 2 High-pass | `BB_EFFECT_HIGHPASS` | `FREQUENCY` (20), `RESONANCE` (0.707) |
| 3 Band-pass | `BB_EFFECT_BANDPASS` | `FREQUENCY` (1000), `RESONANCE` (1) |
| 4 Peak EQ | `BB_EFFECT_PEAK` | `FREQUENCY` (1000), `RESONANCE` (1), `GAIN` dB (0) |
| 5 Low shelf | `BB_EFFECT_LOWSHELF` | `FREQUENCY` (200), `GAIN` dB (0) |
| 6 High shelf | `BB_EFFECT_HIGHSHELF` | `FREQUENCY` (4000), `GAIN` dB (0) |
| 7 Echo | `BB_EFFECT_ECHO` | `DELAY` s (0.3, up to 4), `FEEDBACK` (0.4), `DAMPING` (0.3, low-pass on repeats), `MIX` (0.5) |
| 8 Reverb | `BB_EFFECT_REVERB` | `SIZE` (0.5), `DAMPING` (0.5), `WIDTH` (1), `PREDELAY` s (0), `MIX` (0.3) |
| 9 Compressor | `BB_EFFECT_COMPRESSOR` | `THRESHOLD` dB (-12), `RATIO` (4), `ATTACK` s (0.01), `RELEASE` s (0.2), `GAIN` dB (0) |
| 10 Limiter | `BB_EFFECT_LIMITER` | `CEILING` dB (-0.3), `RELEASE` s (0.05) |
| 11 Distortion | `BB_EFFECT_DISTORTION` | `DRIVE` (0.5), `MIX` (1) |
| 12 Lo-fi | `BB_EFFECT_LOFI` | `RATE` Hz (8000), `BITS` (8) |

Later, if asked for: chorus/flanger, pitch shift, convolution reverb from a sound file.

### Listener-wide 3D settings

`CreateListener` stays as it is. These change the same settings afterwards, on the listener that exists, without freeing
it or creating a second one. The ones with `fade_ms` glide to the new value, so flying from the atmosphere into space
can take the doppler down over a few seconds instead of in one step:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ListenerRolloff factor#[, fade_ms%=0]` | The rolloff of `CreateListener`. |
| `ListenerDoppler scale#[, fade_ms%=0]` | The doppler scale of `CreateListener` (0 off). |
| `ListenerDistance scale#[, fade_ms%=0]` | Meters per world unit. |
| `SpeedOfSound meters#[, fade_ms%=0]` | Default 340, as now (`BB_SPEED_OF_SOUND`). |
| `ListenerRadius radius#[, fade_ms%=0]` | How big the listener is, in world units (default 0, a point as now). See *Listener and source radius*. |
| `ChannelRadius channel, radius#` | How big the source of an emitted channel is (default 0). |
| `ListenerFalloff mode%` | The falloff curve for all 3D channels, playing ones included (`SetFalloff` only changes channels that start later). |
| `GetListenerRolloff#()`, `GetListenerDoppler#()`, `GetListenerDistance#()`, `GetSpeedOfSound#()` | What they are at now. |
| `ChannelDoppler channel, scale#` | Per-channel multiplier on top of the listener's (default 1), e.g. 0 for a radio the player carries. |
| `ListenerAirAbsorption amount#` | Distant emitted sounds lose high frequencies: a low-pass per 3D channel whose cutoff falls with distance. 0 (default) is off. |

All of these also work before `CreateListener`, on the default listener at the origin.

### Listener and source radius

Today the doppler shift is worked out between two points. The shift follows the speed along the line from the listener
to the source, and when a source passes close by, that line turns around within a few milliseconds: the pitch jumps
from high to low (in the CreateListener samples, 535 Hz to 375 Hz) as fast as the 10 ms smoothing lets it. Real
listeners and sources are not points, so a radius makes the turn take longer.

With `ListenerRadius` and `ChannelRadius`, `r` is the sum of both (in world units). The direction used for the speeds
becomes the offset divided by `sqrt(distance² + r²)` instead of by the distance:

```
offset    = source - listener
toward    = offset / sqrt(|offset|² + r²)     ; was offset / |offset|
shift     = from (listener speed · toward) and (source speed · toward), as now
```

Far away (distance much larger than `r`) nothing changes. Close by, the speeds along the line shrink toward 0, so the
shift fades to none at the centre and grows again on the other side. A source passing at speed `v` swings from high to
low over about `2r / v` seconds: 0.1 s for `r` = 3 m at 60 m/s, instead of a few milliseconds. The result is continuous,
so the 10 ms smoothing stays as it is.

The same `toward` is used for panning, so a source passing through the listener moves across the speakers over that
time instead of jumping from one side to the other. Volume is not changed by the radius; the falloff curves are already
flat near the listener.

`r` = 0 (the default) gives exactly today's numbers, so programs that don't set a radius sound the same.

No `FreeListener` is added: `FreeEntity` on the listener already does that, as in the original, and the wiki page of
`CreateListener` will say so. With the setters above, freeing the listener is only needed to move it to another entity
(or use `EntityParent`).

### Example: planet and space segments

```blitzbasic
Include "<audio.bb>"

Global listener = CreateListener(camera, 1, 1, 1)   ; planet: 1 unit = 1 meter, real doppler
Global world    = CreateAudioBus()
Global thin     = AddAudioEffect(world, BB_EFFECT_LOWPASS)

Function EnterSpace(seconds# = 3)
	Local ms = seconds * 1000
	ListenerDistance 50, ms                      ; 1 unit = 50 meters out here
	ListenerRolloff 0.2, ms                      ; ships stay audible far away
	ListenerDoppler 0.1, ms                      ; a hint of shift, as a game effect
	AudioEffectParam thin, BB_EFFECTPARAM_FREQUENCY, 2500, ms ; cockpit sound only, no air outside
End Function

Function EnterAtmosphere(seconds# = 3)
	Local ms = seconds * 1000
	ListenerDistance 1, ms
	ListenerRolloff 1, ms
	ListenerDoppler 1, ms
	AudioEffectParam thin, BB_EFFECTPARAM_FREQUENCY, 20000, ms
End Function
```

The listener settings are phase 1 and the low-pass is phase 3 (see *Phases*), so a game that only needs the listener
part gets it first.

### Example: a cave and a pause menu

```blitzbasic
Include "<audio.bb>"

Global world = CreateAudioBus()           ; game sounds
Global music = CreateAudioBus()           ; music, never muffled
Global cave  = AddAudioEffect(world, BB_EFFECT_REVERB)
AudioEffectParam cave, BB_EFFECTPARAM_MIX, 0 ; dry outside
Global muffle = AddAudioEffect(world, BB_EFFECT_LOWPASS)

SoundBus footsteps, world
SoundBus gunshot, world
ChannelBus PlayMusic("theme.ogg", 1), music

Function EnterCave()
	AudioEffectParam cave, BB_EFFECTPARAM_SIZE, 0.85
	AudioEffectParam cave, BB_EFFECTPARAM_MIX, 0.4, 500  ; fade in over half a second
	ListenerDoppler 0.5
End Function

Function LeaveCave()
	AudioEffectParam cave, BB_EFFECTPARAM_MIX, 0, 800
	ListenerDoppler 1
End Function

Function OpenPauseMenu()
	AudioEffectParam muffle, BB_EFFECTPARAM_FREQUENCY, 600, 200
	AudioBusVolume world, 0.5, 200
End Function
```

## "Scenes": snapshots or plain fades

The request says "per-scene". Two ways to get there:

1. **Fades only (proposed).** Every parameter and bus volume can fade, so a "scene" is a function in the program that
   sets what it needs, as in the example. Nothing more to learn, and the program decides what a scene is.
2. **Snapshots.** `mix = CreateAudioMix()`, `AudioMixParam mix, effect, name$, value#`, `AudioMixVolume mix, bus, v#`,
   `ApplyAudioMix mix, fade_ms`, like FMOD Studio snapshots. Saves a few lines per scene, costs six more commands and
   rules for what happens when two snapshots overlap. If snapshots are wanted, they hold the listener settings above
   too, so that "planet" and "space" can each be one snapshot.

A third idea, reverb zones (an entity with a radius whose effect settings blend in as the listener walks in), builds on
either and is left for later.

## How it is mixed

Nothing changes until a program creates a bus, adds an effect, or sets a send. Until then no `MIX_Group` and no
callback exists, so SDL3_mixer takes its `skip_group_mixing` path and the output is bit-identical to today.

Once something is used:

1. Each bus other than master gets a `MIX_Group`. Its post-mix callback copies the group's buffer into the bus' own
   buffer and clears the group buffer, so SDL3_mixer adds nothing for it. Channels on the master bus stay in SDL3_mixer's
   default group.
2. A send sets a cooked callback on the channel's track. It adds the channel's audio (after gain and pitch), panned the
   same way the channel is, times the send level, into the target bus' buffer.
3. The mixer's post-mix callback walks the bus tree from the leaves up: run the bus' effect chain on its buffer, apply
   its volume, add it into its parent's buffer. The master bus' chain runs last, on the final mix.

Because the effect chains run in the final callback, on buffers that are always the full block length, reverb and echo
tails ring out after the last sound on a bus has stopped. A bus with no sounds and no tail (all effects report silence
for a block) is skipped.

Bus pause/stop go through the runtime's own channel list (it knows which channels are on which bus) and call
`MIX_PauseTrack` etc. per channel, as `PauseChannel` does now.

### DSP

The effects are written in the runtime (`code_runtime/source/sound_effects.c`), not taken from SDL3_mixer (it has none)
and not from SoLoud's sources (decided, see *Decisions*). SoLoud's filters were never reachable from Blitz3D code, and
they are written against SoLoud's own `Filter`/`FilterInstance` classes and sample layout, so using them would mean
rewriting them anyway. The algorithms are standard and public:

- Filters and EQ: biquads with the coefficients from Robert Bristow-Johnson's *Audio EQ Cookbook*.
- Echo: a delay line with feedback and a one-pole low-pass in the loop.
- Reverb: the Freeverb layout (8 comb + 4 all-pass filters per channel, public domain), with a pre-delay line.
- Compressor and limiter: peak follower with attack/release, gain computed in dB.
- Distortion: `tanh` wave shaper. Lo-fi: sample-and-hold plus bit reduction.

With more than two device channels, filters, EQ, echo, dynamics and distortion run on every channel; the reverb reads a
mix of all channels and writes its wet signal to the front pair only. Surround reverb can come later.

Parameter changes come from the program thread while the audio thread runs. Each parameter is an atomic target plus
fade time; the audio thread ramps toward it per sample (at least 5 ms, so even an instant change does not click), and
biquad coefficients are recomputed per block of 32 samples while a fade runs. Adding or removing buses and effects
takes `MIX_LockMixer` for a moment, which is how the runtime already changes tracks.

Cost estimate (not measured): a stereo Freeverb at 48 kHz is about 24 filters × 2 channels × 48 000 samples, a few
million multiply-adds a second, well under 1% of one core. Biquads are cheaper still. Benchmarks on a physical machine
go into the implementation PRs.

### Channel effects and air absorption

Buses and channels both have effect chains (decided, see *Decisions*), with the same effect types and parameters.
A bus effect works on everything on the bus and keeps ringing after its sounds stop; a channel effect works on one
sound and ends with it. Occlusion is the usual case: each emitter behind a wall gets its own low-pass, set from the
program's own line-of-sight test:

```blitzbasic
ch = EmitSound(engine, ship)
Global wall = AddChannelEffect(ch, BB_EFFECT_LOWPASS)
...
If EntityVisible(camera, ship) Then cutoff = 20000 Else cutoff = 800
AudioEffectParam wall, BB_EFFECTPARAM_FREQUENCY, cutoff, 150
```

A channel's chain runs in the cooked callback of its track: after gain and pitch, before the stereo gains of
`bb_channel_apply`, in the track's own format. It is a few filters on one sound, so a channel chain costs a fraction of a
bus chain; a game with 64 occluded emitters runs 64 biquads. The chain ends when the channel does, and so does a reverb
or echo tail on it; put a channel on a bus with the effect when the tail should ring out. Its effect handles are freed
with the channel, and commands on them afterwards behave like channel commands on a channel that has ended.

`ListenerAirAbsorption` is a low-pass the runtime puts in front of every emitted channel's chain, with the cutoff moved
by `bb_channel_follow` from the distance. Sends take the channel's audio after its chain. A channel with no chain, no
air absorption and no send has no callback, as today.

## Compatibility

- The audio commands of the original and `CreateListener`/`EmitSound` keep their behavior and their output, sample
  for sample, as long as no new command is called.
- `CreateListener` keeps its meaning. The new `Listener*` commands change the same three values it sets.
- `FreeEntity` on the listener and a new `CreateListener` keep working as they do now and in the original.
- New command names follow the same rule as every earlier BlitzLLVM addition: a program that defines its own function
  with one of these names keeps calling its own.
- Programs from the original never see a bus, so nothing about channel handles, `ChannelPlaying` or the channel slot
  reuse in `bb_play` changes.

## Testing

- Offline rendering, like `tools/render_doppler_samples.py` and `tools/render_falloff_samples.py`: an impulse through
  the reverb (tail length and decay), a sweep through each filter (−3 dB point within a few percent of the setting),
  echo repeats at the right times and levels, the limiter never above its ceiling.
- Tail test: one short sound on a bus with reverb; the output after the sound ends is not silent for the length of the
  tail.
- Bit-identity test: the existing audio tests render the same output before and after the change.
- Radius: a source passing through the listener at 60 m/s with `r` = 3 swings in pitch over about 0.1 s and pans
  across without a jump; with `r` = 0 the render matches today's `doppler_on.wav`.
- Fades: a parameter step produces no sample-to-sample jump above a threshold.
- Wiki: a page *Audio buses and effects* under the language additions, one page per command as usual, with
  before/after recordings in the media folder.

## Phases

1. Listener: `ListenerRolloff/Doppler/Distance` and `SpeedOfSound` with fades, `ListenerFalloff`, the getters,
   `ChannelDoppler`, and `ListenerRadius`/`ChannelRadius`. On its own this covers the planet/space case, so it comes first.
2. Buses: `CreateAudioBus`, `FreeAudioBus`, `AudioBusParent`, `AudioBusVolume`, pause/resume/stop, `ChannelBus`,
   `SoundBus`.
3. Effects: the chain, parameters, fades, bypass, and the twelve effect types. `<audio.bb>`.
4. Channel effect chains (`AddChannelEffect`), sends, `ListenerAirAbsorption`.
5. If wanted: snapshots and reverb zones.

## Open questions

1. **Snapshots?** Proposed: no, fades are enough (see *"Scenes"*). Snapshots can be added later without changing the
   rest.

## Decisions

- **Effects on buses and on channels** (Xaymar, 26 Nov 2026, "keep things flexible"). First answered as buses only,
  but occlusion needs a filter per channel anyway, so channels get the same effect chains as buses (`AddChannelEffect`)
  instead of a one-off `ChannelLowPass`.
- **Parameters by numbered constant** (Xaymar, 26 Nov 2026), not by name: faster, and the shipped `<audio.bb>` gives
  the numbers names.
- **Own effects** (Xaymar, 26 Nov 2026). The effects are written in the runtime. SoLoud's filters were never reachable
  from Blitz3D code, so there is nothing to stay compatible with.
